extracted.intended_audience: federal agency officials, administrative law practitioners, policymakers, and members of the public interested in administrative procedure
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and organizational requirements for developing, adopting, publishing, and promoting Administrative Conference of the United States (ACUS) recommendations and Statements to improve administrative procedure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose / statutory function
rubrics_metrics.description: One of ACUS's primary statutory functions is to make recommendations for action by federal agencies, the President, Congress, and the Judicial Conference of the United States to improve administrative procedure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations should aim to improve administrative procedure and be addressed to relevant governmental actors (federal agencies, the President, Congress, Judicial Conference).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation development process
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations are developed by committees of ACUS members, typically with the support of expert consultants and ACUS staff.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Drafting should be committee-driven and may rely on expert consultants and ACUS staff for research and drafting support; committees are the primary vehicles for preparing recommendation texts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Adoption / plenary approval
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations are adopted by the full membership at twice-yearly plenary sessions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Formal adoption by full membership at a plenary is required for a proposal to become an ACUS Recommendation; timing and plenary consideration are essential parts of the process.

rubrics_metrics.name: Publication and official distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Adopted recommendations are published on the ACUS website and in the Federal Register.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure recommendations are prepared for public dissemination (website posting and Federal Register publication) so agencies, stakeholders, and the public can access them.

rubrics_metrics.name: Follow-up / implementation encouragement
rubrics_metrics.description: The Chairman and ACUS staff undertake activities to encourage federal agencies to carry out recommendations adopted by ACUS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: ACUS's role includes outreach and encouragement after adoption—plans for promoting uptake by agencies (communications, briefings, engagement) are a component of recommendation work.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statements (versus Recommendations)
rubrics_metrics.description: ACUS sometimes adopts “Statements,” which express the agency's views on a particular matter without making a formal recommendation. Statements are developed through the same process as recommendations but typically set forth issues, conclusions from a study, or comments, rather than recommendations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When the goal is to articulate views, issues, or conclusions rather than to instruct or recommend specific action, use a Statement; Statements follow the same committee and adoption process but differ in substance and intended effect (ACUS has adopted 20 statements).

rubrics_metrics.name: Recommendation metadata and public record
rubrics_metrics.description: Each listed item includes project, recommendation number, adopted on date, committee, and an executive summary, and provides a Download link.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommendations should include clear metadata (project name, recommendation number, adoption date, sponsoring committee) and be accompanied by downloadable full texts for transparency and reference.

rubrics_metrics.name: Executive summary content and function
rubrics_metrics.description: Executive Summaries explain the recommendation’s purpose and identify best practices or guidance (examples: identifying best practices for making government records available; explaining the nature and uses of temporary rules; describing organization of adjudication offices).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An executive summary should succinctly state the problem, scope, and the core recommended practices or conclusions so readers and agencies can quickly understand the recommendation's intent and practical implications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Topical suitability / scope
rubrics_metrics.description: Recommendations address discrete administrative-procedure topics (examples shown: Obtaining Government Records for Use in Agency Proceedings; Temporary Rules; Organization, Management, and Operation of Agency Adjudication Offices; Federal Agency Collaboration with State, Tribal, Local, and Territorial Governments; Agency Investigative Procedures; Consultation with State, Local, and Tribal Governments; Public Participation in Agency Adjudication; Choice of Forum for Judicial Review of Agency Rules; Individualized Guidance; Senate-Confirmed Officials and Administrative Adjudication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Topics should be tightly connected to improving administrative procedures and practice; selection of topics reflects practical problems agencies encounter and areas where guidance or best practices can improve process and outcomes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Archiving and navigability (listing and pagination)
rubrics_metrics.description: The recommendations are presented in a browsable list with pagination (1, 2, 3... Last » Next) and each entry links to more detail and a downloadable text.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Maintain an accessible archive structure (numbering, pagination, and direct download links) so users can locate past recommendations, track adoption dates, and retrieve full texts.
